Sons and Chief Men of Benjamin.<div eID="gen5302" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5303" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3703"/><hi type="bold">1. Now Benjamin begat, &c.--</hi>This chapter contains some supplementary particulars in addition to what has been already said regarding the tribe of Benjamin (see on <reference osisRef="1Chr.7.6">1Ch 7:6</reference>). The names of many of the persons mentioned are different from those given by Moses--a diversity which may be accounted for in part on grounds formerly stated, namely, either that the persons had more than one name, or that the word "sons" is used in a loose sense for grandsons or descendants. But there are other circumstances to be taken into account in considering the details of this chapter; namely, first, that the genealogies of the Benjamites were disordered or destroyed by the almost total extermination of this tribe (<reference osisRef="Judg.20.11-Judg.20.48">Jud 20:11-48</reference>); secondly, that a great number of Benjamites, born in Assyria, are mentioned here, who returned from the long captivity in Babylon, and established themselves--some in Jerusalem, others in different parts of Judea. There were more returned from Babylon of the families belonging to this tribe than to any other except Judah; and hence many strange names are here introduced; some of which will be found in the list of the restored exiles (compare <reference osisRef="Ezra.2.1-Ezra.2.70">Ezr 2:1-70</reference>). <div eID="gen5303" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3704"/><div sID="gen5304" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3704"/><hi type="bold">6. these are the sons of Ehud--</hi>most probably the judge of Israel (<reference osisRef="Judg.3.15">Jud 3:15</reference>). His descendants, who had at first been established in Geba in Benjamin, emigrated in a body under the direction of Gera (<reference osisRef="1Chr.8.7">1Ch 8:7</reference>) to Manahath, where their increased numbers would find more ample accommodation. Manahath was within the territory of Judah. <div eID="gen5304" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3705"/><div sID="gen5305" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3705"/><hi type="bold">8. Shaharaim begat children in the country of Moab--</hi>He had probably been driven to take refuge in that foreign land on the same calamitous occasion that forced Elimelech to emigrate thither (<reference osisRef="Ruth.1.1">Ru 1:1</reference>). But, destitute of natural affection, he forsook or divorced his two wives, and in the land of his sojourn married a third, by whom he had several sons. But there is another explanation given of the conduct of this Benjamite polygamist. His children by Hushim are mentioned (<reference osisRef="1Chr.8.11">1Ch 8:11</reference>), while his other wife is unnoticed. Hence it has been thought probable that it is Baara who is mentioned under the name of Hodesh, so called because her husband, after long desertion, returned and cohabited with her as before. <div eID="gen5305" type="x-p"/>

Ner begat Kish--</hi>The father of Ner, though not mentioned here, is stated (<reference osisRef="1Chr.9.35">1Ch 9:35</reference>) to have been Jehiel. Moreover, the father of Kish is said (<reference osisRef="1Sam.9.1">1Sa 9:1</reference>) to have been Abiel, the son of Zeror, whence it would seem that Abiel and Ner were names of the same person.<div eID="gen5308" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5309" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Abinadab--</hi>the same as Ishui (<reference osisRef="1Sam.14.49">1Sa 14:49</reference>).<div eID="gen5309" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5310" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Esh-baal--</hi>that is, Ish-bosheth. <div eID="gen5310" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain:
33. Ner begat Kish-- The father of Ner, though not mentioned here, is stated ( 1Ch 9:35 ) to have been Jehiel. Moreover, the father of Kish is said ( 1Sa 9:1 ) to have been Abiel, the son of Zeror, whence it would seem that Abiel and Ner were names of the same person.

 Abinadab-- the same as Ishui ( 1Sa 14:49 ).

 Esh-baal-- that is, Ish-bosheth.
